scope: first half of changed items in file order: numbers 1-14 (27 changed in all; numbers[14] included so the half is covered whether the split rounds up or down)

checked.label: 83.7% projected to get free in their lifetime
checked.source: PMC3227547 full text (efetch): abstract and Results give 83.7% lifetime, 3.0% first year, 18.4% at 10 years; n=6,937 of 43,093; Discussion: men less likely to remit; Limitations: institutionalized people not sampled, overestimation. Quote word for word.

checked.label: About 30 tries (daily smokers, Ontario)
checked.source: PMC4908897 full text: Table 3 daily column (n=1092) 6.8 / 20.4 / 29.5 / 142.3; overall n=1277; interviews 2005-2011; Method 3 text 11% first, 5% second observed try; Method 4 peak after several tries. Quote cells word for word.

checked.label: 3-5% of unaided tries lasted 6-12 months; most within 8 days
problems: Headline says 'most slips came within eight days'; the source says 'most relapse occurs in the first 8 days'. In quit-smoking language a slip is a single lapse, which the source did not time; the card's own basis.measured already says relapse. All figures, n, quote (15 words, word for word) and basis otherwise match the PubMed abstract.

fix.headline: Slipping is the norm: 3–5% of tries without help lasted six months to a year; most relapses came within eight days.

checked.label: 12 vs 12 in 100 (cut down first vs stop at once)
checked.source: PMC6953262 full text (PMC HTML): SoF row 12 per 100 vs 12 per 100 (11 to 14), 9219 (22 RCTs); 51 trials, 22,509; 29 USA, 5 China, 13 Europe; search 29 Oct 2018; mean 23 cpd; pharmacotherapy subgroup (fast-acting NRT or varenicline). English trial 22.0% vs 15.5% at 6 months, 697 smokers, nurse support and NRT both arms: PubMed 26975007 abstract.

checked.label: 23 vs 10 in 100 (varenicline vs dummy pill)
checked.source: PMC10169257 full text (efetch): SoF row 99 per 1000 vs 230 per 1000 (213 to 249), 17,395 (41 studies); SAEs 27 vs 33 per 1000; 75 trials, 28 USA; search April 2022; strictest abstinence, biochemical where available. Quote word for word (24 words).

checked.label: Counselling vs brief advice, per 100
problems: Big figure '10 vs 7' and headline 'at least 10' use the low end of the review's range. The source's own arm figures (summary-of-findings table, no-pharmacotherapy row) are 7 per 100 and 11 per 100 (10 to 12); 'at least' treats a confidence limit as a floor.

basis.who: 'not wanting to quit did not rule anyone out' says more than the source. The review took any smokers, but some of its trials recruited only people willing to quit (e.g. 'Clinic attenders willing to accept treatment').

fix.headline: One-to-one counselling: about 11 in 100 smokers expected to stay off six months, against 7 in 100 with brief advice.
fix.basis.measured: Not smoking at least six months later: face-to-face counselling of 10 minutes or more (most much longer, many with follow-up calls) against brief advice, usual care or leaflets. The review's table gives 11 in 100 for counselling, likely between 10 and 12.
fix.basis.who: smokers in trials where no one was offered quit medicine (pregnant women and teen-only trials left out); across the review, 19 of 49 trials recruited hospital patients, and the review did not require people to want to quit
fix.ref.quote: Numbers quit in control condition | Numbers quit after individual counselling … No systematic pharmacotherapy … 7 per 100 | 11 per 100 (10 to 12)

checked.source: PMC6464359 full text (PMC HTML): SoF 'Smoking cessation at longest follow-up - 6 months or more / No systematic pharmacotherapy': 7 per 100, 11 per 100 (10 to 12), RR 1.57, 11,100 (27 RCTs); plain-language 'between 10 and 12 in 100'; 49 trials ~19,000; 30 USA; May 2016; 'Any smokers, except pregnant women'; teen-only excluded. New quote 22 words, cells word for word.

checked.label: Anxiety fell from week 1 (dependent quitters)
problems: Headline 'Anxiety did not rise after quitting' is firmer than the source, which says 'There was no evidence of an increase in anxiety' in 70 people. Everything else (n 70 of 101, DSM-III-R dependence, lapse-free abstinence, 2 weeks before to 4 weeks after, St George's London, randomized trial per PubMed type) matches; quote word for word, 26 words.

fix.headline: No sign that anxiety rose after quitting: in people hooked on nicotine who stayed off, it fell from the first week.

checked.label: Years 1 and 3: quitters rated life and mood better
problems: The study compared change from baseline. Quitters already rated their life higher before quitting (QOLI total 2.45 vs 2.27, p=.03, Table 3), so part of 'rated their life better' is where they started. The caveat says only that quitters may differ in other ways. Figures, n (376 vs 649; 359 vs 640, Table 2), quote (23 words, word for word) and the rest of basis match.

fix.caveat: Quitters weren't chosen at random, so they may differ in other ways: they already rated their life a little higher before quitting. Life satisfaction slipped for everyone, but less for quitters; the authors call the differences modest. Quitting made no difference to marriage satisfaction.

checked.source: PubMed 22160762 abstract; full text PMC3298628 (efetch): Methods (Madison and Milwaukee, Jan 2005-June 2007, >9 cigs/day, six counselling sessions, CO-confirmed), Tables 2-4, Discussion ('modest').

checked.label: Half free about 26 years after it began (projected)
checked.source: PMC3227547 full text: 'Half of the cases of nicotine, alcohol, cannabis and cocaine dependence remitted approximately 26, 14, 6 and 5 years after dependence onset'; quote cut to nicotine with ellipses, word for word; remission defined as 'finally stopped ... never started happening again'; males lower hazards.

checked.label: 10 vs 7 in 100 with rewards
problems: Both figures are modelled, not counted: the summary-of-findings table gives 71 per 1000 (no rewards) and 108 per 1000 (rewards), the second worked out from the first with the combined effect; the plain-language summary rounds that to 10. The headline ('were off') reads as a head count, and unlike the other what-helps cards (stop vs cut, varenicline, counselling) the caveat does not say so. Figures, n (18,303 in 39 trials), quote (26 words, word for word), 48 trials / 33 USA, November 2023 and the lasting-effect point all match.

fix.caveat: The 7 in 100 is the typical rate in the trials' no-reward groups; the 10 in 100 is the review's summary figure, worked out from it with the combined effect (its table gives 108 in 1,000), not counted in one group. In most trials a program ran the rewards and checked people's breath or urine. A private bet with a friend was not what was tested.

checked.source: PMC11725379 full text (PMC HTML): plain-language summary and SoF 1 (71 vs 108 per 1000, 18,303 (39 RCTs)); subgroup on follow-up after incentives ended (RR 1.46, 32 studies).

checked.label: 4-5 kg, most in the first three months
checked.source: PubMed 22782848 abstract: untreated means 2.85 / 4.23 / 4.67 kg at 3 / 6 / 12 months, 16/37/34/13% estimated; full text PMC3393785: n 514 (25), 1138 (19), 183 (5), 174 (3) at month 12; 59 of 62 trials North America, Europe or Australia. Quote 29 words, word for word; 'gain slowed' follows from the monthly means.

checked.label: At least 1 in 4 men's erections improved
checked.source: PubMed 15610111 abstract: 118 stopped vs 163 continued; '> or = 25% of ex-smokers but in none of the current smokers'; risk factors excluded; requested NRT; IIEF-5 before and after 1 year; older and advanced ED improved less; Tehran affiliation. Quote word for word.

checked.label: About 81 in 100 never used any help
checked.source: PMC8154113 full text (efetch): Table 5 'Any treatment services' lifetime any NUD 18.75, severe 27.78; 12-month 20.34; prevalence 20.0% (12-month) and 27.9% (lifetime); n=36,309; weighted cross-tabulations; help types match Table 5 rows. 81 = 100 - 18.75, said with 'about'. Quote word for word, 15 words.

checked.label: About 90 in 100 stayed off each later year
checked.source: PMC2577779 full text (PMC HTML): annual relapse 10% (95% CI 5-17%) after dropping outlier Tonnesen 1988; 8 RCTs of NRT, follow-ups 2-6 yrs; 4-33 per group, 31-96 per study; CO confirmed in all but Blondal 1989; no treatment after 1 yr; 41% after 5 yrs; NHANES 1982-84 (1990 Surgeon General report) 14% and 10%, then <5%. Countries not given in the paper. 90 = 100 - 10 with 'about'; per-year wording and caveat keep it from reading as a lifetime share. Quote 27 words, word for word.
